sections.what: The Restoration Team repairs homes for vulnerable Houston homeowners. Volunteers and partners address disaster damage, unsafe structures and accessibility barriers. Its repair and recovery work helps families preserve a safe place to live.
sections.monitoring: Current applications are closed while the queue is served, with reopening anticipated January 2027. The homepage reports cumulative 565 families and 100,000 volunteer hours since 2017; older 275-family copy is inconsistent. The VEVOR story reports priority repairs for the 500th family but remaining work before return to occupancy. A goal of 100 families annually by 2028 is not current annual throughput. Request dated unique completed homes, hazards resolved, occupancy timing, actual cash savings and worker/material opportunity costs.
sections.qualitative: Current repair stories show concrete safety and accessibility work. Volunteers, congregations and material partners provide practical delivery capacity. Original latest returns and expense-side event costs identify a transparent annual denominator. Cumulative families and volunteer hours do not establish annual completions or causal health gains. Applications are currently closed; added gifts are not demonstrated to overcome project-capacity limits. Unrecognized volunteer and partner resources, alternative funding and household savings remain uncertain. Current official giving page and original return confirm The Restoration Team, EIN 83-2427982, Houston. Current giving route was checked without a transaction. Donated equipment and professional services must not be counted as both free inputs and household retail benefits.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $68.09 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 0.097278 clinical QALYs and 0.019262 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.001469 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $793,541. Annual 50 repair-household opportunities are a judgment, not an observed annual count. Full annual response .4 gives 20 exposed households after alternative contractors, insurance, disaster aid and partner replacement. The same union supplies clinical .3 meaningful safety/comfort response, .02 utility for one finite year, with full .001 safety harm per exposed household. This is an unsupported acute safety/comfort prior, not repair-trial calibration or mortality. Independent .5 resource success receives $600 net otherwise-paid repair, temporary displacement or care costs actually avoided, after maintenance and alternative support. Positive overlap .5 precedes full $100 one-time disruption, foregone time and process burden; successful households net $200 and others lose $100. No house value or retail repair-value multiplier enters resources. Union 20 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 6; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $25,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Outside volunteer labor, donated equipment and partner time are unknown economic resources centrally, not free. Larger annual-cost and explicit provider-incidence cases stress them. Insurance/public-budget replacement or displaced beneficiaries require matched payer incidence; existing recipient costs are not charged twice. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: FY2025 tax expenses $787,489 plus $6,052 netted direct event cost gives $793,541. FY2024 $1,019,204 plus $6,564 gives $1,025,768. FY2023 $889,875 has no populated event expense. Schedule D audited/donated expense reconciliation lines are unpopulated, not evidence of zero volunteer opportunity costs. Recognized whole recipient annual resources versus the narrow hypothetical repair channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal donor price.

model.costScope: Whole annual recognized recipient resources versus conditional repair safety and cash-resource channel; outside volunteer labor, other programs and next gift unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Houston repair delivery; judged .98 metro share applied once
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Insurance, public disaster aid, city repair programs, paid contractors, other nonprofits and family/partner work retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Completed safer and more accessible homes, finite safety/comfort improvement and actual net avoided household costs; not cumulative families, volunteer hours or retail repair value
